excerpt: Paano magtanim ng sweet corn? Here is how traditional Filipino farmers usually plant mais na matamis (corn, sweet), step by step from getting the field ready to the harvest, with the day of each step and what to change for a higher yield.

heroImage.alt: A cornfield on a hillside in Pilar, Capiz, its leaves drying close to harvest

blocks.title: This is the traditional way
blocks.text: This guide shows how traditional farmers usually plant mais na matamis. Use it as a starting point. For a higher yield, update it: plant certified seed or clean planting material, test your soil, and follow the right spacing and fertilizer.

How Filipino farmers grow sweet corn for fresh ears sold in markets and by the roadside. Most use hybrid seed bought each crop and pick the ears about two and a half months after planting.

Before you plant, get the field ready with our [land preparation guide for corn](/land-preparation/corn-land-preparation). Then choose your seed or planting material with the [mais na matamis varieties sold here](/crop-varieties/corn). If the leaves turn pale later on, the [mais na matamis nutrient deficiency guide](/nutrient-deficiencies/corn-nutrient-deficiency) helps you find what is missing. For more on the crop, read [pagtatanim ng mais in Tagalog](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-mais).
When to plant mais na matamis

Grown all year where water is available. Rainfed growers plant at the start of the rains, around May to June, and many plant again from October to January, when there is less disease and the ears fill well with watering.
What you plant

Hybrid seed bought new every crop. The seed is small and wrinkled and needs moist, warm soil and a shallow planting. Some growers sow in seedling trays and set the young plants out after about two weeks to save on costly seed.
Paano magtanim ng sweet corn, step by step
The crop is ready about 75 days after sowing.
Before planting (Bago magtanim)

items.title: 14 days before sowing: Plow and harrow
items.text: Plow once and harrow two times to get a fine, loose seedbed. Many growers spread chicken manure before the last harrowing.

items.title: 1 day before sowing: Open the furrows

blocks.text: Planting day (Pagtatanim)

items.title: Sowing day: Fertilizer in the furrow
items.text: Drop complete fertilizer (14 14 14) in the furrow and cover it with a little soil.

items.title: Sowing day: Plant the seed shallow
items.text: Drop one seed every 20 to 25 cm and cover it with only 2 to 3 cm of moist soil, since sweet corn seed rots if buried deep in wet ground.

blocks.text: Care while it grows (Pag aalaga)

items.title: Day 1: Water after planting
items.text: If the soil is dry, run water into the furrows or water by hand so the seed comes up evenly.

items.title: Day 7: Replant the misses
items.text: Replant empty hills within the first week so the plants ripen together.

items.title: Day 14: Off barring and weeding
items.text: Plow lightly between the rows with the soil thrown away from the plants, then hand pull the weeds in the rows.

items.title: Day 18: Look into the whorls
items.text: Check the whorls for fall armyworm and corn borer damage every few days, since sweet corn is their favorite.

items.title: Day 22: Side dress urea
items.text: Drop urea (46 0 0) beside the plants on moist soil.

items.title: Day 24: Hill up
items.text: Plow toward the rows to cover the fertilizer and firm the plants against wind.

items.title: Day 45: Water well through silking
items.text: Keep the soil moist from tasseling until the ears fill. Dry soil now gives ears with missing kernels.

blocks.text: Harvest (Anihan)

items.title: Day 70: Pick the fresh ears
items.text: Harvest about 18 to 22 days after the silks appear, when the silks are brown and dry and a pressed kernel gives milky juice. Pick in the cool early morning.

items.title: Day 70: Sell or cool the same day
items.text: Keep the picked ears in the shade and get them to the buyer the same day, since the sweetness fades quickly in the heat.

blocks.text: Spacing, water and fertilizer for mais na matamis
Spacing
Rows about 75 cm apart with one plant every 20 to 25 cm.
Water
Needs steady moisture. In the dry season growers run water into the furrows about once a week, more often in sandy soil, and never let the field dry out from tasseling to harvest.
Fertilizer

Chicken manure at land preparation if available, complete fertilizer (14 14 14) in the furrow at planting, and urea (46 0 0) at about three weeks before hilling up. Some growers give a little more urea at tasseling. To read what a bag really gives, see our guide to [fertilizer for this crop](/blog/increase-corn-yield-per-hectare).
Care and harvest
Care while it grows

Off barring at about two weeks and hilling up at about three to four weeks, with hand weeding in the rows. Growers check the whorls often for fall armyworm and corn borer, which hit sweet corn harder than field corn.
When and how to harvest
Sweet corn is picked fresh, about 65 to 75 days after planting, when the silks are dry and brown and the kernels are full and milky. The ears are sold or cooked within a day.
Common mistakes when planting mais na matamis

items: Burying the seed too deep in wet soil, so much of it rots before it comes up.
Planting next to field corn that flowers at the same time, which makes the kernels starchy and less sweet.
Letting the soil dry out at silking, which gives ears with gaps.
Picking too late, when the kernels have turned doughy and starchy.
Leaving picked ears in the sun for hours before selling.

blocks.text: How to get a higher yield of mais na matamis
The traditional way gets a crop, but small changes add up. These are the first things to change, one season at a time.

items: Buy fresh seed of a variety suited to your season and plant into moist, fine soil.
Keep sweet corn away from other corn, or plant it so it flowers at least two weeks apart.
Feed by a soil test and split the nitrogen into two or three doses.
Scout every few days for fall armyworm and act while the larvae are small.
Plant in small batches every two weeks so you have ears to sell over a longer time.

items.q: When do farmers plant mais na matamis in the Philippines?
items.a: Grown all year where water is available. Rainfed growers plant at the start of the rains, around May to June, and many plant again from October to January, when there is less disease and the ears fill well with watering.

items.q: How far apart do you plant mais na matamis?
items.a: Rows about 75 cm apart with one plant every 20 to 25 cm.

items.q: How long before mais na matamis can be harvested?
items.a: It is ready about 75 days after sowing. Sweet corn is picked fresh, about 65 to 75 days after planting, when the silks are dry and brown and the kernels are full and milky.

items.q: What do you plant to grow mais na matamis?
items.a: Hybrid seed bought new every crop. The seed is small and wrinkled and needs moist, warm soil and a shallow planting.
